transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Lee. Well, I'm here because I just keep making these really dumb mistakes at work. I supervise a sales team, and lately on our sales reports, I'll do things like... copy the wrong numbers straight off the team dashboard. Or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I'm supposed to be checking. 

The frustrating part is that it happens even when I thought I already went over it and checked my work. It's just getting to be a real problem for me.
How long has this been going on—weeks, months, or longer?
Well, definitely longer than a few weeks. I'd say it's been a real problem since I moved into this supervisor role. That was about... a year and two months ago, roughly.
How has your sleep been lately—are you having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested when you wake up?

Um, no, my sleep is actually pretty fine. I don't really have any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, honestly. I usually wake up feeling normal... rested enough, I guess. So, yeah, no real issues there.

Did you have similar problems with attention, forgetfulness, or careless mistakes back in school or earlier jobs, before this supervisor role, or is this something new that started around the time you were promoted?

No, it's definitely not new. I was like this as a kid, too. Honestly, my mom still brings up the notes my teachers used to send home in elementary school. They were always saying things like how I rushed through my work, or how I was always losing my homework. And it wasn't just the work, either—they'd say I was always talking out of turn, or that I couldn't just stay in my seat unless someone reminded me to sit down. So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
Outside of work, do you notice similar issues—like losing things, being forgetful, or interrupting people—in your daily life or relationships?

Yeah, it definitely spills over into my personal life. At home, it causes a lot of arguments, honestly. My wife and my friends... they get frustrated because they feel like they can't count on me to follow through on things I say I'll do. I forget stuff we talked about, or I just don't finish things I start around the house. And at work, like I said, it's bad. It actually got to the point where my manager put it in my formal performance review recently. So, yeah, it's definitely affecting both sides of my life.
Have you been feeling down, anxious, or excessively worried lately, in a way that's separate from these attention and forgetfulness issues?

No, not really. I mean, sure, I get stressed or frustrated when I drop the ball at work or when my wife gets mad at me. But that's all tied to... well, the forgetting and the mistakes. Outside of that, I don't feel down or just generally anxious about things. So, yeah, I'd say no to that.
